U.S. is likely to strike Iranian targets in retaliation after Iran attacked commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz this week. - Axios 

Attacks

•	Iran’s IRGC fired at least two missiles at commercial ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz Monday night.

•	Both vessels suffered significant damage but no casualties.

•	A tanker was hit by an unknown projectile near Oman’s Limah, causing a fire.

•	One targeted vessel appears to be an LNG tanker operated by Qatar’s Nakilat.

•	The IRGC attacked a third commercial ship Tuesday morning.

Context

•	Indirect U.S.-Iran talks in Doha last week ended without progress on the Strait of Hormuz issue.

•	The attacks could complicate ongoing negotiations to end the U.S.-Iran conflict.

Chinese AI models are winning U.S. enterprise usage as OpenAI and Anthropic costs rise.

Usage shift

•	U.S. companies sent more than 30% of token consumption to Chinese models every week since Feb. 8.

•	That share peaked at 46%.

•	Chinese models had only 4.5% of token traffic in the first half of 2025.

•	They averaged 11% over the prior twelve months.

Cost gap

•	Open-source Chinese models run 60% to 90% cheaper than leading U.S. alternatives.

•	Z.ai’s GLM-5.2 came within one percentage point of Anthropic’s Opus 4.8 on a benchmark.

•	GLM-5.2 cost about one-fifth as much.

Adoption signals

•	Vercel said GLM-5.2 led every model it tracked in 2026 for speed of adoption.

•	In its first full week, daily token volume grew about 27x.

NATO industry forum delivers new defence deals.

Saab

•	NATO will begin formal negotiations on up to 10 GlobalEye aircraft.

•	Saab CEO Micael Johansson said deliveries could start as soon as 2030.

•	He put the final price at roughly $400 million to $450 million per aircraft.

Lockheed Martin / Rheinmetall

•	The companies signed a memorandum of understanding to jointly produce ATACMS missiles in Germany.

•	That would be the first manufacture of the missile outside the U.S.

•	The U.S. will also establish a Europe maintenance facility for PAC-3 missiles.

Northrop Grumman

•	NATO allies will buy up to five MQ-4C Triton surveillance drones.

•	Norway, Finland, Germany, and Denmark signed a letter of intent.

Airbus and MTU Aero Engines plan a joint venture to develop a fully electric hydrogen fuel cell engine.

•	The agreement is non-binding.

•	It is subject to standard regulatory approvals.

•	It also depends on completion of social processes at European and national levels.

•	The new joint venture is expected to start operations in 2027.

Markets are pricing inflation down, but borrowing costs may stay high.

Inflation outlook

•	Treasury bond prices imply 2.3% annual inflation over the next five years.

•	That is down from the recent peak of 2.7% in May.

•	The 10-year breakeven has fallen to about 2.2% from 2.4% in early June.

Real rates

•	Five-year real yields have jumped to 1.9% from 1.3% since early May.

•	Ten-year real yields have climbed to 2.2% from 1.9%.

•	Benchmark Treasury yields are still around 4.5%.

Rate-sensitive sectors

•	Mortgage rates have hovered near 6.6% in recent weeks.

•	That is above the 6% rate in late February before the attack on Iran.

What’s driving it

•	A big driver is capital demand from the AI buildout.

SK Hynix’s $28 billion US listing is drawing multiple times its available shares in demand ahead of Thursday pricing.

•	The offering has drawn strong early demand from global long-only funds and technology-focused investors.

•	SK Hynix will sell 17.79 million new shares as American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) on the Nasdaq.

•	The company trimmed its fundraising target to about $28 billion, down from an earlier goal of $29 billion, after a recent share price decline.

•	Major investors including Baillie Gifford Overseas, Coatue Management, and Situational Awareness Partners have separately indicated interest in buying up to a combined $7 billion of the ADRs.

•	The offering is led by Bank of America, Citigroup, Goldman Sachs, and JPMorgan.
